mentl/ad8546f:
driver_collect_dag seeds "prelude" before the entry whenever fs_exists finds
it. Same wheel, same harness, same program, same path form, varying only
whether that seed can resolve: 0.71s with the mentl-home mapping, 0.03s
without it. THE SEED IS THE WHOLE FLOOR -- 0.68 of 0.71s -- and 149 x 0.68 =
101s of the sweep's 257s CPU is that seed, re-run for programs that
reference none of it.

TWO EARLIER READINGS WERE CONFOUNDED, corrected here rather than quietly
kept. The first compared a DIRECT wasmtime invocation on stdin against the
SHIM on a path -- two harnesses, not two link paths. Re-measured on one
harness the shim costs nothing (direct-path 0.72s, shim-path 0.72s), so the
conclusion survived but the reasoning had not earned it. The second ran from
a lib-less directory expecting the seed to skip; MENTL_HOME still resolved
and the flat 0.75s proved nothing either way. Removing the resolution ROOT is
what isolates it, and that is the measurement that counts.

THE SEED MAY NOT BE DELETED. Its comment says why and it is correct: every
module speaks the prelude's vocabulary -- map, fold, Option, FeedbackSpec --
with no import line, and without the seed a compile emits a module that
cannot assemble. The fix is to make it demand-driven, not absent.

THE DESIGN is the arc this wheel already ran one layer down. Parse the ENTRY
first, which 0.03s buys; take its free-name set; pull only the prelude decls
providing those names, transitively. That wants a name-to-decl index over the
prelude that does not parse bodies -- a header scan -- which is the same shape
as lower's demand worklist, where a name popping from the frontier constructs
its decl and a dead decl never constructs. The retry-on-miss alternative
(link bare, re-link on E_MissingVariable) is rejected: it halves the cost for
programs using nothing and DOUBLES it for every program that touches the
prelude, which is most of the sweep.

Stamp complete: traced, one writer enumerated, priced at 0.68s per invocation
